## Natural history notes

A small meadow katydid characterized by its slender green to brownish body, very long antennae, and reduced or absent wings, giving it a short-bodied, flightless appearance compared with many other katydids. In Florida, it is found in grassy wetlands, marsh edges, wet prairies, damp fields, roadside ditches, and other open habitats with dense grasses, sedges, or rushes. It feeds mainly on grasses and other soft plant material, sometimes taking small insects, and remains hidden low in vegetation where its shape and coloration help it avoid predators.
